title: One Client Too Many
briefing: Case study, inspired by the collapse of a single over-leveraged client that hurt the banks around it in 2021. Marrowby Pharma is Valtren's biggest client and growing fast.
Rafe Dunmore loves it. Hollis Varga has noticed Marrowby paying later every quarter. Before the new risk appetite is signed off, size the exposure.

evidence.title: Revenue by client
evidence.body: Valtren revenue: 48,000,000. Marrowby Pharma: 31% of it.

evidence.title: Credit control report
body: Marrowby's receivables: 3,600,000, and paying in 75 days against 30 in the contract.
Rumours in the trade press about Marrowby's debts.

evidence.title: Dedicated assets
evidence.body: Twelve trailers leased solely for Marrowby, with 1,200,000 of lease payments left, which Valtren owes whatever happens.

questions.prompt: How much revenue a year comes from Marrowby?
If Marrowby failed tomorrow, what is Valtren's immediate loss exposure (money owed plus commitments it cannot walk away from)?
questions.explanation: 3,600,000 receivables + 1,200,000 lease commitments = 4,800,000. Lost future revenue is a separate, strategic hit.

mistakes.feedback: That is a year of revenue. The immediate loss is what Marrowby owes plus the commitments Valtren cannot exit.
Receivables are most of it, but the dedicated trailer leases have to be paid too.

questions.prompt: What do you recommend to the executive?

options.label: Set a client concentration limit in the appetite, tighten Marrowby's terms, insure the receivable and diversify growth
options.feedback: Keeps a profitable client while capping the damage if it fails.

options.label: Exit the Marrowby contract before it gets worse
options.feedback: That trades a risk for a certain loss of 31% of revenue.

options.label: Keep growing with Marrowby: the margin pays for the risk
options.feedback: Margin does not help if the client cannot pay; exposure would grow further.

options.label: Ask credit control to watch payment days monthly
options.feedback: Monitoring is part of it, but it changes nothing about the exposure.

questions.prompt: Rate the risk of Marrowby failing to pay, given the evidence.
questions.explanation: Stretching payment days and debt rumours make it possible; a 4.8 million hit with 31% of revenue at stake is severe.

questions.prompt: Which are early warning signs of client credit risk? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Payment days stretching quarter after quarter
One client's share of revenue rising quickly
Trade press reports about the client's debts
The client placing larger orders
options.feedback: Bigger orders can come from a healthy or a struggling client; on its own it is not a warning.

lesson: Concentration turns one client's problem into yours. Measure exposure as what you would lose tomorrow, cap it in the appetite, and act on the early signals.
